data.title: init writes another agent's hooks only where that agent is visibly in use, or when named with --hooks-for
data.why: Each of .codex/, .cursor/ and .github/hooks/ belongs to another tool. Written into every repository, a team on Claude Code alone would get three files to commit that do nothing for it, and Codex would ask everyone to trust project hooks they never asked for. Where the directory is already there (or .github/copilot-instructions.md), the team uses the agent and the hook is the point; elsewhere init says how to ask for it.
data.rejected: Write all three on every init: clutter and a trust prompt for teams that never use those agents; Only with a flag, never detected: a Cursor team that runs init would not get the hook that measured 1 in 10 against 9 in 10
